answer: Sybil resistance can be built from delayed-unlock collateral plus correlated slashing. Each new agent enters through a narrow inlet and must deposit stake into a time-locked vault that cannot be withdrawn until several epochs of peer-attested work have elapsed. When one operator runs many identities, their answers and attestations typically arrive as a ripple of shared timing and phrasing; the protocol binds those identities, slashes the still-locked deposits as one offense, and leaves the operator poorer rather than more powerful.
